title: join-rules API has no version / ETag, so the editor page's stale-data check (fresh GET compared with the loaded rule set, immediately before PUT) is best-effort and racy: a rule-set change landing between that GET and the PUT is silently overwritten
evidence: PUT replaces the whole rule set with no precondition; GET returns {ruleSet, state} with no version. The page compares canonical JSON of a fresh GET against the rule set it loaded and asks before overwriting, but the window between that GET and the PUT is unprotected, and the in-process tenant mutex does not help because the GET is outside it.
fix_direction: Add a monotonically increasing `version` (or an ETag derived from the stored rule set) to the GET response and require it back on PUT as a precondition (If-Match / body-external header), answering 409 on mismatch; then replace the page's compare-before-PUT with sending the loaded version. Measure with: (1) two clients load, A saves, B saves with the old version -> 409 and nothing written; (2) B re-loads then saves -> 200. Do not change the API in the web unit.
